projectName: Procedural 3D Coin Pusher and Slot Machine
description: A feature-rich 3D arcade Coin Pusher game that incorporates standard, gold, giant, and bonus coins. The project runs procedural sound synthesis and procedural particle generation dynamically via code to completely bypass external asset dependencies. It includes a physics-based slider (pusher), dynamic side barrier walls, a timing-based slot machine pocket system on the pusher itself, and real-time UI/camera feedback mechanisms.

scripts.responsibility: Handles camera shake physical reactions during intense impact events (such as Giant Coin drop) with automatic scene startup self-attachment capabilities.
Defines Coin types, manages physics properties, alters visuals (colors/scale/mass) based on classification, self-destructs safely, and notifies triggers of enter/exit events.
Detects screen inputs (taps/drags) to drop coins at configured X axes, executes fever-mode rapid coin drops, and rolls random coin types.
Initializes and runs procedural, asset-free particle systems on demand for coin spawns, scoring zones, and side losses.
Controls core game states (scores, inventory, fever level, active durations) and coordinates updates across spawning, side barrier wall mechanics, and UI.
Handles kinematic movement of the pusher using sine-wave oscillation to physically push coins forward on the stage.
Detects coins arriving at the primary front scoring exit and forwards corresponding score events to the GameManager while protecting against double detection.
Tracks and processes coins falling off left/right side gutters with sound and impact effects without rewarding point increments.
Controls dynamic physical barriers to temporarily prevent coins from falling into side gutters during specific game bonuses.
Runs a timing-based slot machine game by injecting triggers dynamically onto the pusher and rendering results on procedural 3D billboards.
Registers collisions inside the dynamically generated pusher slot pockets to trigger the slot reel rotation sequence.
Synthesizes real-time retro game audio waveforms (sine waves, arpeggios, and frequency slides) entirely via code to avoid audio clip asset dependencies.
Updates game screens dynamically (text overlays, fever sliders, next coin prediction indicators, and game over overlays) with procedural fallback creation routines.
